rationale_evidence.statement: Completed 18-chapter tier table: T4 KERNEL stays at 2 (Ch1 Sanjaya->Omega corpus-native; Ch13 Kshetrajna->N not-in-K, R5, FA-4[E], but also T0 for its rival 7-type ontology, K=f(F,A_t), and error E1); T3 stays 8; T2 rose 5->6; T1 correspondence fell ~37->~32; T0 refuted/RX rose 8->14. Final conclusion: new kernel primitives from the Gita = 0, canonical relations = 0; the Gita CONSTRAINS the kernel, it does not POPULATE it. Reading the chapters directly did not add candidates -- it moved six from T1 to T0, because the register listed terms while the chapters contained formalizations that type-check badly.

[S2103]

Three checkable type errors in 'solved' Gita-chapter formalizations, invisible from the correspondence register (which lists terms, not formalizations): E1 (Ch13 3.3) K_supreme = sup(Omega) is ill-formed because sup requires an order on Omega, but 0 of 5 ratified Sigma axes carries an established order (per Step 291) and (Omega,F,P) does not exist (per gap G-22). Completed 18-chapter tier table: T4 KERNEL stays at 2 (Ch1 Sanjaya->Omega corpus-native; Ch13 Kshetrajna->N not-in-K, R5, FA-4[E], but also T0 for its rival 7-type ontology, K=f(F,A_t), and error E1); T3 stays 8; T2 rose 5->6; T1 correspondence fell ~37->~32; T0 refuted/RX rose 8->14. Final conclusion: new kernel primitives from the Gita = 0, canonical relations = 0; the Gita CONSTRAINS the kernel, it does not POPULATE it. Reading the chapters directly did not add candidates -- it moved six from T1 to T0, because the register listed terms while the chapters contained formalizations that type-check badly. [S2222]
